topic_ko: 장기 기억을 들여다보는 좁은 창, 작업 기억
_note: 원문 유형은 글의 순서(주어진 글→(C)→(B)→(A)). order 유형을 가장 강하게 출제. 유형마다 passage 를 다르게 paraphrase.

passage: The major difference between working memory and long-term memory is one of awareness.
We are consciously aware of what sits in working memory, but we cannot reach into long-term memory directly.
Instead, we pull information out of long-term storage and into working memory in order to use it.
For instance, you are not now picturing every actor you have ever watched on screen.
Those memories rest in long-term storage, well outside your consciousness.
Yet if asked to name them, you would draw them, one by one, into working memory and recite them.
Working memory makes this possible, though it can hold only about seven items at a time.
choices: why long-term memory eventually replaces working memory as we age
how actors are remembered more easily than ordinary people
how forgetting protects the brain from holding too many memories
how we reach long-term memories only by pulling them into limited working memory
why working memory can store an unlimited amount of information
theme.explanation_ko: 장기 기억엔 직접 접근할 수 없고, 그 정보를 의식이 가능한 작업 기억으로 끌어와야 쓸 수 있으며 작업 기억은 약 7개로 한정된다는 내용. ④가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ①장기 기억의 대체, ②배우 기억의 용이성, ③망각의 보호 기능, ⑤무한 저장은 본문의 핵심이 아니다.

passage: We should not imagine that everything stored in our minds is always before our eyes.
We are aware only of what is in working memory, never of long-term memory itself.
To use a stored memory, we must first bring it into working memory.
We ought to understand that consciousness is just a narrow window onto a vast store.
You are not now aware of every actor you have seen, yet you could list them if asked.
They wait in long-term memory until working memory retrieves them one by one.
We must therefore respect the limits of working memory, which holds only about seven items.
Knowing how memory really works helps us study and think more wisely.
choices: 우리는 작업 기억을 통해서만 장기 기억에 접근할 수 있음을 알아야 한다.
장기 기억은 작업 기억보다 훨씬 빨리 사라진다.
기억력을 높이려면 한 번에 많은 정보를 외워야 한다.
의식은 우리가 가진 모든 기억을 동시에 보여 준다.
배우의 이름은 다른 정보보다 기억하기 쉽다.
claim.explanation_ko: 장기 기억에는 직접 접근할 수 없고 작업 기억으로 끌어와야 한다는 사실을 이해해야 한다는 주장. ①이 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ②소멸 속도, ③대량 암기, ④동시 인식, ⑤배우 이름은 본문 주장과 어긋나거나 지엽적이다.

passage: Working memory and long-term memory differ above all in awareness.
We notice what is in working memory, but long-term memory stays out of direct reach.
We get at it only by moving its contents into working memory.
Right now, for example, you are not aware of all the actors you have ever seen.
They sit in long-term memory, beyond your consciousness.
Asked to name them, you would haul them into working memory and rattle them off.
But remember: working memory can hold only about seven items at once.
choices: 장기 기억은 한 번에 일곱 개의 정보만 저장할 수 있다.
의식은 모든 장기 기억을 항상 또렷이 보여 준다.
배우의 얼굴은 이름보다 기억하기 쉽다.
우리는 작업 기억으로 정보를 끌어와야만 장기 기억을 의식할 수 있다.
작업 기억은 용량 제한이 전혀 없다.
gist.explanation_ko: 장기 기억은 직접 의식되지 않고, 그 정보를 작업 기억으로 끌어와야 의식·사용할 수 있다는 것이 요지. ④가 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ①용량 주체 혼동, ②항상 의식, ③얼굴, ⑤무한 용량은 요지가 아니다.

passage: There is a quiet wall between what we can sense in our minds and what merely lies stored.
Working memory is the lit room we stand in; long-term memory is the dark archive behind it.
We cannot read that archive directly; we must carry its files into the lit room first.
You are not now thinking of every actor you have seen, though all of them are filed away.
Ask for the list, and you fetch them, one at a time, into the light of working memory.
There you can finally see and name them.
But the lit room is small: it holds only about seven things at once.
choices: Why We Forget the Faces of Famous Actors
Long-Term Memory: A Storehouse with Unlimited Doors
How to Train Your Brain to Recall Seven Things
The Day Consciousness Replaced Memory Forever
Working Memory: The Narrow Window onto a Vast Memory Store
title.explanation_ko: 장기 기억(거대한 저장고)을 들여다보는 좁은 창으로서의 작업 기억을 압축한 ⑤가 제목.
title.distractor_ko: ①망각, ②무한한 문, ③암기 훈련법, ④의식의 대체는 글의 초점이 아니다.

passage: The deepest difference between working and long-term memory is one of awareness.
We can sense what is in working memory, but long-term memory lies beyond direct reach.
We access it only by carrying its contents into working memory.
Right now you are not aware of every actor you have ever seen on screen.
They are filed away in long-term memory, outside the light of your consciousness.
But if asked, you would bring them into the light one by one and name them.
Working memory, however, is a small lamp: it lights only about seven things at once.
implication.underlined: Working memory, however, is a small lamp
choices: memories slowly fade unless they are kept warm and bright
the brain physically glows when we try hard to remember
long-term memory is brighter and clearer than working memory
we can recall actors only when the room is well lit
working memory can illuminate only a few items at any one time
implication.explanation_ko: '작업 기억은 작은 등불'이라는 비유는 작업 기억이 한 번에 소수의(약 7개) 항목만 비출 수 있음을 뜻한다. ⑤가 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ①퇴색, ②뇌의 발광, ③밝기 비교, ④실제 조명은 비유의 의미와 다르다.

passage: The big difference is that we is aware of working memory but cannot directly access long-term memory.
We reach long-term memory by bringing its information into working memory.
For example, right now you are not aware of all the actors that you have ever seen.
They are stored in your long-term memory, outside your consciousness.
However, if I asked you to list them, you would use working memory to retrieve them one by one.
Your working memory can access your long-term memory and bring those memories to awareness.
But remember that it has a limit of seven items or chunks.
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
grammar.explanation_ko: ① 주어 'we'(1인칭 복수)에는 be동사 'are' 가 와야 하므로 'we is aware' 는 수일치 오류이다. 'are aware' 로 고쳐야 한다. ①이 정답.
grammar.distractor_ko: ②전치사 by + 동명사 bringing, ③목적격 관계대명사 that, ④가정법 would use, ⑤조동사 can 뒤 동사원형 bring 은 모두 옳다.

passage: The big difference is that we are aware of working memory but cannot directly access long-term memory.
We reach long-term memory by removing its information into working memory.
For example, right now you are not aware of all the actors you have ever seen.
They are stored in your long-term memory, hidden outside your consciousness.
However, if I asked you to list them, you would use working memory to retrieve them one by one.
Your working memory can access long-term memory and bring those memories to awareness.
But remember that it has a limit of seven items or chunks.
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
vocab.explanation_ko: ② 장기 기억의 정보를 작업 기억으로 '가져옴(bringing)'으로써 그것에 도달한다는 흐름인데 '제거함(removing)'은 정반대 의미라 부적절하다. bringing 으로 고쳐야 한다. ②가 정답.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①access(접근하다), ③stored(저장된), ④retrieve(인출하다), ⑤bring(가져오다)은 문맥에 적절하다.

passage: Working memory and long-term memory differ most of all in awareness.
We sense what is in working memory, yet we cannot reach long-term memory directly.
We get at long-term memory only by __________.
For example, you are not now aware of every actor you have ever seen.
They are stored in long-term memory, outside your consciousness.
Asked to name them, you would pull them into working memory one by one.
But working memory is limited: it holds only about seven items at a time.
blank.blank_target: We get at long-term memory only by
choices: erasing the items we no longer need
expanding working memory without any limit
storing new memories as quickly as possible
bringing its contents into working memory
ignoring the information already in our minds
blank.explanation_ko: 배우 예시처럼 장기 기억의 내용을 작업 기억으로 '끌어와야(bringing into working memory)' 비로소 의식·사용할 수 있다. ④가 정답.
blank.distractor_ko: ①지우기, ②무한 확장, ③빠른 저장, ⑤무시하기는 본문 흐름과 맞지 않는다.

irrelevant.intro: The big difference between working and long-term memory is that we are aware of working memory but cannot directly access long-term memory.
sentences: We access long-term memory only by bringing its information into working memory.
For example, right now you are not aware of all the actors you have ever seen on screen.
Regular physical exercise has been shown to improve mood and overall heart health.
However, if asked to list those actors, you would retrieve them into working memory one by one.
But remember that working memory has a limit of about seven items or chunks.
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
irrelevant.explanation_ko: 글은 '장기 기억은 작업 기억으로 끌어와야 의식된다'는 흐름인데 ③ '규칙적 운동의 기분·심장 건강 효과'는 무관하다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ①②④⑤는 모두 장기·작업 기억의 접근 방식과 한계라는 흐름에 연결된다.

order.given: The big difference between working and long-term memory is that we are explicitly aware of the information in working memory, but we are not able to directly access the information in our long-term memory. We access long-term memory by bringing the information into working memory.

blocks.A: Your working memory can thus access your long-term memory and bring those memories to awareness. But remember it has a limit of seven items or chunks.
blocks.B: However, if I asked you to list all the actors, you would use your working memory to retrieve them one by one and reel them off.
blocks.C: For example, right now you are not aware of all the actors you have ever seen. They are stored in your long-term memory outside your consciousness.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글의 일반 진술을 (C)가 'For example' 로 배우 예시를 들고, (B)가 'However' 로 그 배우들을 작업 기억으로 인출하는 상황을 잇고, (A)가 'thus' 로 작업 기억의 기능과 7개 한계로 마무리한다. (C)-(B)-(A) = ⑤.
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 'thus ... 한계'는 결론이므로 먼저 올 수 없고, (B)의 'However' 는 (C)의 '의식하지 못한다'는 진술 뒤라야 자연스럽다.

insert.insert_sentence: However, if I asked you to list all the actors, you would use your working memory to retrieve them one by one.

passage_marked.text: We access long-term memory only by bringing its information into working memory.
For example, right now you are not aware of all the actors you have ever seen.
They are stored in your long-term memory, outside your consciousness.
Your working memory can thus bring those long-term memories to awareness.
But remember that it has a limit of only seven items or chunks.

choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장은 'However ... 배우들을 나열하라면 작업 기억으로 인출한다'로, 배우들이 의식 밖 장기 기억에 저장돼 있다는 ③ 다음, 작업 기억이 그 기억을 의식으로 가져온다는 일반화 앞에 와야 한다. ③이 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: ③에 넣지 않으면 'Your working memory can thus bring those memories to awareness' 의 'thus' 가 받을 인출 과정이 앞에 나타나지 않는다.

passage: Working memory and long-term memory differ chiefly in awareness.
We sense working memory directly, but long-term memory stays beyond direct reach.
We reach it only by drawing its contents into working memory.
You are not now aware of every actor you have seen, though all are stored away.
Asked to name them, you would pull them into working memory one at a time.
There you could finally see and recite them.
But working memory holds only about seven items at once.
summary.summary_template: We cannot reach long-term memory directly; we must __(A)__ its contents into working memory, which can hold only a __(B)__ number of items.
summary.explanation_ko: 장기 기억은 그 내용을 작업 기억으로 (A)가져와야(bring) 하고, 작업 기억은 (B)제한된(limited, 약 7개) 수만 담는다. ④.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 erase/hide 가 아니라 bring, (B)는 unlimited/huge/growing 이 아니라 limited 여야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 우리는 정보를 작업 기억으로 가져옴으로써 장기 기억에 접근한다.
writing.answer: We access long-term memory by bringing the information into working memory.
writing.explanation_ko: by + 동명사 bringing(~함으로써), into working memory(작업 기억 안으로).

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 그것들은 너의 의식 밖 장기 기억에 저장되어 있다.
writing.answer: They are stored in your long-term memory outside your consciousness.
writing.explanation_ko: 수동태 are stored + 장소 in your long-term memory + outside your consciousness.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 하지만 그것이 일곱 개의 항목이라는 한계를 가지고 있다는 것을 기억하라.
writing.answer: But remember that it has a limit of seven items.
writing.explanation_ko: 명령문 remember + that절 + a limit of seven items(일곱 개라는 한계).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름상 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: Asked to name the actors, you would use working memory to ___________ them one by one and reel them off.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: We are explicitly aware of the information in working memory, but we are not able to directly access the information in our long-term memory.
writing.answer: 우리는 작업 기억 속의 정보를 명확히 의식하지만, 장기 기억 속의 정보에는 직접 접근할 수 없다.
writing.explanation_ko: explicitly aware of(~을 명확히 의식하는), not able to directly access(직접 접근할 수 없는).
